body.text: sāṃkhyasūtravivaraṇam |
body.translated_text: <s>Sāṃkhyasūtravivaraṇam</s> (Commentary on the Sāṃkhya Sūtras).

body.text: śrīkapilāya namaḥ |
body.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Śrī Kapila</s>.

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self), in the <s>Sāṃkhya Sūtra</s> is composed
a brief commentary for the removal of non-discrimination.

body.text: iha khalu bhagavān kapilo munirāsuraye 'nukampayā pañcaviṃśatitattvānyupadiśya sūtrayāmāsa |
body.translated_text: Here indeed, the blessed sage <s>Kapila</s>, having taught the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s> (principles) to <s>Āsuri</s> out of compassion, composed the sūtras.

children.translated_text: Eight are the <s>prakṛtis</s> (primal causes) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 1 ||

body.text: aṣṭau prakṛtaya ityādi / kāḥ punastā ityucyante / pradhānaṃ mahānahaṃkārastanmātrāṇi ca / pradhānaṃ prakṛtiravyaktamavyākṛtaṃ cetyanarthāntaram / mahān mahattatvaṃ buddhiradhyavasāyalakṣaṇam / ahaṃkāro 'bhimānalakṣaṇo vaikṛtikastaijaso bhūtādiśceti trividhaḥ / tanmātrāṇi tu pañca śabdatanmātramākāśahetuḥ / sparśatanmātraṃ vāyuyoniḥ / rūpatanmātraṃ tejoyoniḥ / rasatanmātramapprakṛtiḥ / gandhatanmātraṃ pṛthivīhetuḥ / iti pañcatanmātrāṇi ityaṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ /
body.translated_text: "Eight are the <s>prakṛtis</s>" and so forth. What then are they? It is stated: <s>Pradhāna</s> (the primal substance), <s>Mahat</s> (the great one), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), and the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), <s>Avyākṛta</s> (the undifferentiated) — these are synonyms. <s>Mahat</s>, the <s>Mahat-tattva</s>, <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), is characterized by determination. <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>, characterized by ego-sense, is threefold: <s>Vaikṛtika</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Bhūtādi</s>. The <s>tanmātras</s> are five: the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> is the cause of <s>Ākāśa</s> (space); the touch-<s>tanmātra</s> is the source of <s>Vāyu</s> (air); the form-<s>tanmātra</s> is the source of <s>Tejas</s> (fire); the taste-<s>tanmātra</s> is the source of <s>Ap</s> (water); the smell-<s>tanmātra</s> is the cause of <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth). Thus the five <s>tanmātras</s> — these are the eight <s>prakṛtis</s>.

children.translated_text: Sixteen are the <s>vikāras</s> (modifications) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 2 ||

body.text:
ke punarvikārāḥ kati |
ṣoḍaśavikārāḥ |
ekādaśendriyāṇi pañca mahābhūtāni ca |

children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s> (organs of cognition), named ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose, function in perceiving sound, touch, form, taste, and smell.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and generative organ are the <s>karmendriyāṇi</s> (organs of action), functioning in speaking, grasping, locomotion, excretion, and pleasure.
<s>Manas</s> (mind), possessing the dual capacity of knowledge and action, characterized by intention and deliberation — thus these are the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties).
And the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements), characterized as space, air, fire, water, and earth, are five — thus these are the sixteen <s>vikāras</s> (modifications).

body.translated_text: What then are the modifications, and how many? Sixteen are the modifications: the eleven <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties) and the five <s>mahābhūtas</s> (great elements).

children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 3 ||
Now, what is <s>Puruṣa</s>? It is stated:

children.text: puruṣo 'nekastriguṇarahito vivekī aviṣayo 'sādhāraṇo 'prasavadharmā cetanaḥ sākṣī kevalo madhyastho draṣṭā 'kartā ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is many, devoid of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), discriminating, not an object, uncommon, not productive, conscious, a witness, solitary, neutral, a seer, and a non-agent.

body.text: atha ke punastrayo guṇā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: Now, what then are the three <s>guṇas</s>? It is stated:

children.translated_text: The triad of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 4 ||

body.text: traiguṇyaṃ sattvaṃ rajastama iti |

children.translated_text: These three alone are the <s>guṇas</s>, constituting the <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of qualities).

<s>Sattva</s> by name is characterized by sharpness, softness, lightness, clarity, attachment, delight, contentment, desirelessness, satisfaction, and the like; it has infinite varieties and, in summary, brings about happiness.

<s>Rajas</s> by name is characterized by sorrow, affliction, frustration, stupefaction, elation, agitation, anger, pride, and the like; it has infinite varieties and, in summary, brings about suffering.

children.text: tamo nāmācchādanāvaraṇabībhatsadainyagauravālasyanidrāpramādādilakṣaṇamanantabhedaṃ samāsato mohātmakaṃ etat traiguṇyaṃ vyākhyātam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> by name is characterized by concealment, covering, loathsomeness, wretchedness, heaviness, laziness, sleep, negligence, and the like; it has infinite varieties and, in summary, is of the nature of delusion. Thus this <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of qualities) has been explained.

body.translated_text: The <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of qualities) consists of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.

children.translated_text: One should know <s>sattva</s> as illuminating, <s>rajas</s> as activating,

children.text: vināśakaṃ tamo vindyāt traiguṇyaṃ nāma sañjñitam //
children.translated_text: and <s>tamas</s> as destructive — this is called the <s>traiguṇya</s> (triad of qualities).
<s>Sañcara</s> (evolution) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 5 ||
<s>Pratisañcara</s> (involution) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 6 ||

body.text:
atrāha kaḥ sañcaraḥ pratisañcaraśceti |
ucyate |
utpattiḥ sañcaraḥ |
pralayaḥ pratisañcaraḥ |
tatrotpattirnāmāvyaktāt samupadiṣṭāt sarvajagataḥ pareṇa rūpeṇādhiṣṭhānātmakāt mahān mahato 'haṃkāraḥ |
sa ca trividhaḥ |
vaikṛtiko bhūtādistaijasaśceti |
tatra vaikṛtādindriyāṇyutpadyante bhūtādestanmātrāṇi taijasādubhayam indriyāṇi tanmātrāṇi ceti |
tanmātrebhyo bhūtāni |
ayaṃ sañcaraḥ |
pratisañcaro nāma bhūtāni tanmātreṣu līyante |
tanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāhaṃkāre |
ahaṃkāro buddhau |

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) into <s>Avyakta</s> (the unmanifest).

children.text: tato 'vyaktaṃ tu kvacinna līyate kasmāt anutpannatvāt |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Avyakta</s> does not dissolve into anything — why? Because it is unoriginated.
Thus is <s>pratisañcara</s> (involution).
Thus these two — <s>sañcara</s> (evolution) and <s>pratisañcara</s> (involution) — have been explained.

body.translated_text: Here it is asked: what are <s>sañcara</s> and <s>pratisañcara</s>? It is stated: Creation is <s>sañcara</s>. Dissolution is <s>pratisañcara</s>. There, creation means: from <s>Avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), which has been taught as the substratum of the entire world in its transcendent form, arises <s>Mahat</s> (the great one); from <s>Mahat</s> arises <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle). And that is threefold: <s>Vaikṛtika</s>, <s>Bhūtādi</s>, and <s>Taijasa</s>. From the <s>Vaikṛtika</s> arise the sense faculties; from <s>Bhūtādi</s> arise the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements); from <s>Taijasa</s> arise both — the sense faculties and the <s>tanmātras</s>. From the <s>tanmātras</s> arise the elements. This is <s>sañcara</s> (evolution). <s>Pratisañcara</s> means: the elements dissolve into the <s>tanmātras</s>; the <s>tanmātras</s> and sense faculties into <s>Ahaṃkāra</s>; <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> into <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect);

children.translated_text: <s>Adhyātma</s> (pertaining to the self) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 7 ||
<s>Adhibhūta</s> (pertaining to the elements) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 8 ||
<s>Adhidaiva</s> (pertaining to the deities) || <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 9 ||

body.text:
atrāha kiṃvidhamadhyātmamadhibhūtamadhidaivataṃ ca |
atrocyate |
buddhiradhyātmam |
bodhayitavyamadhibhūtam |
brahmā tatrādidaivatam |
ahaṃkāro 'dhyātmam |
abhimantavyamadhibhūtam |
rudrastatrādhidaivatam |
manodhyātmaṃ saṃkalpamadhibhūtam |
candrastatrādidaivatam |
śrotramadhyātmam |
sparśayitavyamadhibhūtam |
vāyustatrādhidaivatam |
cakṣuradhyātmam |
darśayitavyamadhibhūtam |
sūryastatrādidaivatam |
jihvādhyātmam |
rasayitavyamadhibhūtam |
varuṇastatrādhidaivatam |
nāsādhyātmam |
ghrātavyamadhibhūtam |
pṛthivī tatrādhidaivatam |
vāgadhyātmam |
vaktavyamadhibhūtam |
agnistatrādhidaivatam |
pāṇiradhyātmam |
ādātavyamadhibhūtam |
indrastatrādhidaivatam |
pādāvadhyātmam |
gantavyamadhibhūtam |
viṣṇustatrādhidaivatam |
pāyuradhyātmam |
utsraṣṭāvyamadhibhūtam |
mitrastatrādhidaivatam |
upasthamadhyātmam |
ānandayitavyamadhibhūtam |

children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> is the presiding deity there.
Thus the subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and divine (<s>adhidaiva</s>) of the thirteen instruments (<s>trayodaśa karaṇa</s>) have been explained.
What are the four? To this he says "ca" (and).
Three are of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>, and the fourth is the presiding deity — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Here one asks: what is the subjective (<s>adhyātma</s>), the objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>)? Here it is stated: <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) is the subjective; that which is to be cognized is the objective; <s>Brahmā</s> is the presiding deity there. <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) is the subjective; that which is to be appropriated is the objective; <s>Rudra</s> is the presiding deity there. <s>Manas</s> (mind) is the subjective, <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention) is the objective; <s>Candra</s> (Moon) is the presiding deity there. The ear is the subjective; that which is to be touched is the objective; <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) is the presiding deity there. The eye is the subjective; that which is to be shown is the objective; <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) is the presiding deity there. The tongue is the subjective; that which is to be tasted is the objective; <s>Varuṇa</s> is the presiding deity there. The nose is the subjective; that which is to be smelled is the objective; <s>Pṛthivī</s> (Earth) is the presiding deity there. Speech is the subjective; that which is to be spoken is the objective; <s>Agni</s> (Fire) is the presiding deity there. The hand is the subjective; that which is to be grasped is the objective; <s>Indra</s> is the presiding deity there. The feet are the subjective; that which is to be traversed is the objective; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the presiding deity there. The excretory organ is the subjective; that which is to be excreted is the objective; <s>Mitra</s> is the presiding deity there. The generative organ is the subjective; that which is to be enjoyed is the objective;

children.text: catvāri yo vedayate yathāvad guṇasvarūpāṇyadhidaivataṃ ca /
children.translated_text: One who knows the four as they truly are — the natures of the <s>guṇas</s> and the presiding deity,

children.text: vimuktapāpmā gatadoṣasaṅgo guṇāṃstu bhuṅkte na guṇaiḥ sa bhujyate //
children.translated_text: freed from sin, gone beyond the taint of faults, enjoys the <s>guṇas</s> but is not consumed by them.
The five <s>abhibuddhis</s> (modes of awareness). || Tats_10 ||

body.text:
atha kāstā abhibuddhaya ityucyante |
pañcābhibuddhayaḥ |
buddhirabhimāna icchā kartavyaṃ tatkriyā ceti |
abhimukhī buddhirabhibuddhiḥ |
idaṃ karaṇīyametyetadadhyavasāyo buddhiḥ kriyātmaparāmarśasvarūpapratyayaḥ |
abhimukho māno 'haṃ karomītyahaṃkāro 'bhimānaḥ |
buddhikriyā icchā vāñchā |

children.translated_text: <s>Kartavya</s> (duty) is <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention), the function of <s>manas</s> (mind).

children.text: kriyā etadvastusvarūpamiti kartavyālocanaṃ yadbuddhīndriyāṇāṃ sā kriyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kriyā</s> (action) — the examination of the true nature of a thing, "this is what must be considered" — that is the action of the <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (sense organs of cognition).

children.text: itthametat kartavyamiti yatpravṛttiḥ karmendriyāṇāṃ sā kriyeti |
children.translated_text: "This is how this is to be done" — the activity of the <s>karmendriyas</s> (organs of action) is that <s>kriyā</s> (action).
Thus the five <s>abhibuddhis</s> (modes of awareness) have been explained.

body.translated_text: Now, what are those <s>abhibuddhis</s> (modes of awareness)? It is stated: the five <s>abhibuddhis</s> are: <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>abhimāna</s> (self-identification), <s>icchā</s> (desire), <s>kartavya</s> (duty), and <s>kriyā</s> (action). The awareness directed toward an object is <s>abhibuddhi</s>. "This is to be done" — such determination is <s>buddhi</s>, a cognition whose nature is reflection on action. Self-directed identification, "I am doing" — the <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) is <s>abhimāna</s>. The activity of <s>buddhi</s> is <s>icchā</s> (desire), which is longing.

children.translated_text: The five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>). || Tats_11 ||

body.text:
atha kāḥ pañcakarmayonayaḥ ucyante |
dhṛtiḥ śraddhā sukhā avividiṣā vividiṣā ceti pañca karmayonayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, what are the five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>)? They are stated: <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>sukhā</s> (happiness), <s>avividiṣā</s> (desire for non-knowledge), and <s>vividiṣā</s> (desire for knowledge) — these are the five sources of action.

children.translated_text: That conviction which delights in speech, action, and body,
being established in that and grounded in that — this indeed is the characteristic of <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness).
Freedom from envy, celibacy, performing sacrifices, officiating at sacrifices, austerity,
accepting gifts and performing <s>homa</s> (fire offerings) — these are traditionally known as the characteristics of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith).
One who, desiring happiness, pursues learning, rituals, and austerities,
always devoted to expiation — this is declared to be <s>sukhā</s> (happiness).

body.text:
viṣadhūmamūrchitavadavividiṣā |
vividiṣā dhyāyināṃ prajñāyoniḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Avividiṣā</s> (desire for non-knowledge) is like being stupefied by the fumes of poison. <s>Vividiṣā</s> (desire for knowledge) is the source of wisdom for those who meditate.

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca nityaṃ cedamacetanam /
children.translated_text: Oneness and separateness, permanence, and this is insentient,

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ satkāryamakṣobhyaṃ jñeyā vividiṣā hi sā //
children.translated_text: subtle, the effect pre-exists in the cause, unshakeable — this indeed should be known as <s>vividiṣā</s> (desire for knowledge).
<s>Vividiṣā</s> (desire for knowledge), which brings about the capacity for cause and effect, is a natural (<s>prākṛtika</s>) disposition.

children.text: dhṛtiḥ śraddhā sukhā avividiṣā catasro bandhāya vividiṣaikā mokṣāya iti pañca karmayonayo vyākhyātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), <s>sukhā</s> (happiness), and <s>avividiṣā</s> (desire for non-knowledge) — these four lead to bondage; <s>vividiṣā</s> (desire for knowledge) alone leads to liberation — thus the five sources of action (<s>karmayonis</s>) have been explained.
The five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>). || Tats_12 ||
Here one asks: what are the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>)?
It is stated:

children.text: prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaśca udāno vyāna eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> —
these are the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>) in the bodies of embodied beings.

body.text:
tatra prāṇo nāma vāyuryo 'yaṃ mukhanāsikādhiṣṭhānaprāṇanāt krameṇānanāt prāṇa ityabhidhīyate |
apāno nāma vāyurnābheradhiṣṭhātā apanayanādadhogamanāccāpāna ityabhidhīyate |

children.text: samāno nāma vāyurhṛdadhiṣṭhātā samanāt samagamanācca samāna ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: The vital breath called <s>Samāna</s>, seated in the heart, is so called because of its equalizing (<s>samanā</s>) and its uniform movement (<s>samagamana</s>).

children.text: udāno nāma vāyuḥ kaṇṭhādhiṣṭhātā ūrdhvaṃ gamanācca udāna ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: The vital breath called <s>Udāna</s>, seated in the throat, is so called because of its upward movement (<s>ūrdhvagamana</s>).

children.text: vyāno nāma vāyuḥ sandhyadhiṣṭhātā prāṇādijṛmbhaṇācca vyāna ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: The vital breath called <s>Vyāna</s>, seated in the joints, is so called because of its expanding (<s>jṛmbhaṇa</s>) of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the other vital breaths.
Thus the five vital breaths (<s>vāyus</s>) have been explained.

body.translated_text: Among these, the vital breath called <s>Prāṇa</s> is so called because it enlivens (<s>prāṇana</s>) from its seat in the mouth and nose, and because of its gradual breathing (<s>ānana</s>). The vital breath called <s>Apāna</s>, seated below the navel, is so called because of its carrying away (<s>apanayana</s>) and its downward movement (<s>adhogamana</s>).

children.translated_text: The five agents of action (<s>karmātmānaḥ</s>) || <s>Tats</s>_13 ||

body.text:
āha ke te pañcakarmātmānaḥ ucyante |
vaikārikastaijaso bhūtādiśca sānumāno niranumānaśceti |
tatra vaikārikaḥ śubhakarmakartā |
taijaso 'śubhakarmakartā |

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhūtādi</s> is the doer of deluded action.
The <s>Sānumāna</s> is the doer of virtuous-deluded action.
The <s>Niranumāna</s> is the doer of non-virtuous-deluded action.
Thus these five agents of action have been explained.

body.translated_text:
He asks: what are these five agents of action? It is said:
The <s>Vaikārika</s> (modified), the <s>Taijasa</s> (luminous), the <s>Bhūtādi</s> (primal element), the <s>Sānumāna</s> (with inference), and the <s>Niranumāna</s> (without inference).
Among these, the <s>Vaikārika</s> is the doer of virtuous action.
The <s>Taijasa</s> is the doer of non-virtuous action.

children.translated_text: The fivefold <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) || <s>Tats</s>_14 ||

body.text:
āha kā sā pañcaparvāvidyeti |
ucyate |
tamo moho mahāmohastāmisro 'ndhatāmisraśceti |
tatra tamomohāvubhāvetāvaṣṭātmākau |
mahāmoho daśātmakaḥ |
tāmisrāndhatāmisrau cāṣṭādaśātmākau |
tatra tamo nāmāṣṭāsu prakṛtiṣvavyaktabuddhyahaṃkārapañcatanmātrasañjñitāsu anātmasvātmajñānābhimānastama ityabhidhīyate |
moho nāmāṇimādyaṣṭāguṇaiśvaryaprāptaye yobhimāna utpadyate sa moha ityabhidhīyate |

children.text: mahāmoho nāma dṛṣṭānuśravikeṣu viṣayeṣu daśasu nivṛtteṣu mukto 'hamiti manyate sa mahāmoha ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāmoha</s> is defined as: when one thinks 'I am liberated' after the ten objects — both seen and heard of — have ceased, that is called <s>Mahāmoha</s>.

children.text: tāmisro nāma aṣṭaguṇaiśvarye 'ṇimādye daśavidhe ca viṣaye pratihatasya duḥkhamutpadyate 'sau tāmisra ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmisra</s> is defined as: the suffering that arises for one who is thwarted in the eightfold lordly power of <s>Aṇimā</s> and others, and in the tenfold objects — that is called <s>Tāmisra</s>.

children.text: andhatāmisro nāma aṇimādyaṣṭaguṇaiśvarye daśavidhe ca viṣaye siddhe maraṇakāle ca yo viṣādaḥ pratyapadyate so 'ndhatāmisra ityabhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Andhatāmisra</s> is defined as: the despair that arises at the time of death when the eightfold lordly power of <s>Aṇimā</s> and others, and the tenfold objects, have been attained — that is called <s>Andhatāmisra</s>.
Thus this fivefold <s>avidyā</s> with sixty-two divisions has been explained.

body.translated_text:
He asks: what is this fivefold <s>avidyā</s>? It is said:
<s>Tamas</s> (darkness), <s>Moha</s> (delusion), <s>Mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom), and <s>Andhatāmisra</s> (blind darkness).
Among these, <s>Tamas</s> and <s>Moha</s> are each eightfold.
<s>Mahāmoha</s> is tenfold.
<s>Tāmisra</s> and <s>Andhatāmisra</s> are each eighteenfold.
Among these, <s>Tamas</s> is defined as follows: the false identification of the self (<s>ātman</s>) in the eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (evolutes) — designated as <s>Avyakta</s> (unmanifest), <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and the five <s>Tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) — which are not the self, is called <s>Tamas</s>.
<s>Moha</s> is defined as: the pride that arises for the attainment of the eightfold lordly powers such as <s>Aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and others is called <s>Moha</s>.

children.translated_text: The twenty-eightfold incapacity (<s>aśakti</s>) || <s>Tats</s>_15 ||

body.text:
atrāha kāṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiḥ |
atrocyate |
ekādaśendriyavadhāḥ saptadaśabuddhivadhāḥ |
eṣāṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiḥ |
tatrendriyavadhāstāvat |
badhirastvakbadhiraḥ andhaḥ jaḍajihvaḥ ajighraḥ mūkaḥ kuṇiḥ paṅguḥ napuṃsakaḥ ūrdhvavāyuyuktaḥ amanāḥ |
taduktam |
body.translated_text:
Here he asks: what is the twenty-eightfold incapacity?
Here it is said:
Eleven impairments of the sense organs and seventeen impairments of the intellect.
This is the twenty-eightfold incapacity.
Among these, first the impairments of the sense organs:
Deaf, skin-impaired, blind, taste-impaired, smell-impaired, mute, cripple-handed, lame, impotent, one afflicted with upward-moving wind, and mindless.
As stated:

children.translated_text: Deafness, skin-disease, blindness, dullness of taste, loss of smell, likewise,
muteness, crippling of the hands, lameness, impotence, upward wind-disorder, and madness.

body.text:
etedindriyadvārā buddhereva vadhāḥ |
sākṣādbuddhivadhā yathā |
body.translated_text:
These are impairments of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) through the doors of the sense organs.
The direct impairments of the intellect are as follows:

children.translated_text: The ninefold contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) || <s>Tats</s>_16 ||
The eightfold attainment (<s>siddhi</s>) || <s>Tats</s>_17 ||

body.text: navavidhatuṣṭivaikalyāt aṣṭavidhāsiddhavaikalyācca saptadaśabuddhivadhā ityaṣṭāviṃśatidhāśaktiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Due to the deficiency of the ninefold contentment and due to the deficiency of the eightfold attainment, there are seventeen impairments of the intellect — thus the twenty-eightfold incapacity.

body.text:
kā punarnavadhā tuṣṭiḥ ucyate |
catasra ādyātmikyastuṣṭayaḥ bāhyāḥ pañca |
ādyāḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ |
prakṛtyaiva muktiḥ kiṃ punaḥ sādhanairiti tuṣṭiḥ prakṛtyākhyā ambho nāma |

children.translated_text: The contentment that comes from having adopted means such as renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) is called <s>Upādāna</s>-contentment, named <s>Salila</s> (water).

children.text: kālenaiva muktyādikaṃ setsyati kiṃ duḥkhaiḥ saṃnyāsādisādhanairiti tuṣṭiḥ kālākhyā 'gho nāma |
children.translated_text: The contentment that 'liberation and such will come through time alone — what need of painful means like renunciation?' is called <s>Kāla</s>-contentment, named <s>Ogha</s> (flood).

children.text: yā tu bhāgyādeva sarvaṃ setsyati kiṃ sādhanādidhyānādikleśairiti sā bhāgyākhyā tuṣṭirnāma |
children.translated_text: The contentment that 'everything will be accomplished through fortune alone — what need of the exertions of means, meditation, and such?' — that is the <s>Bhāgya</s>-contentment, named <s>Tuṣṭi</s> (satisfaction).

children.text: bāhyāḥ śabdādiviṣayavairāgyāstuṣṭayaḥ arjanarakṣaṇakṣayabhogahiṃsādoṣadarśanaṃ vairāgyahetuḥ pañcavidhastadbhedena pañcatuṣṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The external contentments are dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward objects like sound and others. The perception of the faults of acquisition, preservation, decay, enjoyment, and harm is the cause of dispassion, which is fivefold; by that division, [there are] five contentments.

body.translated_text:
What then is the ninefold contentment? It is said:
Four are internal (<s>ādhyātmikī</s>) contentments, and five are external.
The first [four] are named <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>Upādāna</s> (means), <s>Kāla</s> (time), and <s>Bhāgya</s> (fortune).
The contentment that 'liberation comes through <s>Prakṛti</s> alone — what need of other means?' is called <s>Prakṛti</s>-contentment, named <s>Ambhas</s> (water).

body.text:
atha kāḥ siddhayaḥ ucyante |
aṣṭau siddhayaḥ |
ucyante |
adhyayanaṃ tāraṃ nāma siddhiḥ |
tato 'rthajñānaṃ sutāraṃ nāma |
tatastarkeṇārthaparīkṣaṇaṃ tāratāraṃ nāma siddhiḥ |
tataḥ parīkṣakasaṃvādanaṃ ramyakaṃ nāma |
tato vivekakhyātiḥ sadāmuditaṃ nāma |

children.translated_text: These are the five secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) attainments.
The destruction of the three kinds of suffering — these are the three primary (<s>mukhya</s>) attainments.
They are named <s>Pramoda</s> (delight), <s>Mudita</s> (joy), and <s>Modamāna</s> (rejoicing). The fruit — thus there are eight attainments.
From the opposite of the contentments and attainments, there are seventeen impairments of the intellect.

body.translated_text:
Now, what are the attainments (<s>siddhis</s>)? It is said:
There are eight attainments.
They are stated:
Study (<s>adhyayana</s>) is the attainment called <s>Tāra</s> (delivering).
From that, knowledge of meaning is called <s>Sutāra</s> (well-delivering).
From that, examination of meaning through reasoning is the attainment called <s>Tāratāra</s> (most delivering).
From that, dialogue with examiners is called <s>Ramyaka</s> (delightful).
From that, discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is called <s>Sadāmudita</s> (ever-joyful).

children.translated_text: The ten fundamental topics (<s>mūlikārthāḥ</s>) || <s>Tats</s>_18 ||

body.text:
ke punarmaulikārthāḥ katidhā ucyante |
daśadhā maulikārthāha |
ekatvamarthavattvaṃ pārārthyaṃ pradhānasya |
anyatvamakartṛtvaṃ bahutvaṃ puruṣasya |
astitvaṃ yogo viyogaścetyubhayayoḥ |
śeṣavṛttiḥ pariśiṣṭatvaṃ pralaye tadubhayayoḥ |
body.translated_text:
What then are the fundamental principles, and in how many ways are they stated?
 The fundamental principles are stated in ten ways:
 Oneness, purposefulness, and being-for-the-sake-of-another belong to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).
 Otherness, non-agency, and multiplicity belong to <s>Puruṣa</s> (the self).
 Existence, union (<s>yoga</s>), and separation (<s>viyoga</s>) belong to both.
 Residual activity (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>), meaning remaining in a state of latency during dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), belongs to both of them.

children.translated_text: That has been stated [as follows]:
The existence of <s>Pradhāna</s>, its oneness, its purposefulness, its accordance with reality,

children.text: pārārthyaṃ ca tathā naikyaṃ viyogo yoga eva ca //
children.translated_text: its being-for-the-sake-of-another, and likewise non-identity, separation, and union,

body.text: śeṣavṛttirakartṛtvaṃ maulikārthāḥ smṛtā daśa //
body.translated_text: residual activity, and non-agency — these are remembered as the ten fundamental principles.

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

children.translated_text: The creation of grace (<s>anugrahasarga</s>). <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 19.

body.text:
atrāha ko 'nugrahasargaḥ |
anugṛhṇāti pratyayabhūtādisargaṃ yaḥ sargaḥ so 'nugrahasargaḥ |
tanmātrasarga evāsau viśeṣāparanāmā |
ke viśeṣāḥ kiyantaśca |
ucyante |
liṅgadehāha sthūladehāḥ sthūlabhūtāni ca |
tatra liṅgaṃ sthūladehāt pūrvamutpannamavyāhataṃ sthūlanāśe 'pyanaśvaram |

children.translated_text: It consists of <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), the sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), and the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>).

Pervaded by the dispositions (<s>bhāva</s>) called <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and <s>adharma</s> (vice), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) and passion (<s>avairāgya</s>), sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) and non-sovereignty (<s>anaiśvarya</s>), it transmigrates.

The gross elements (<s>sthūlabhūtāni</s>), however, are the earth-globe, oceans, fire, <s>Śiśumāra</s> (the celestial porpoise constellation), <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (the cosmic egg), <s>Virāṭ</s> (the cosmic body), and so forth.
What are the gross bodies and of how many kinds? It is stated:

body.translated_text:
Here one asks: what is the creation of grace (<s>anugrahasarga</s>)?
 That creation which favors (<s>anugṛhṇāti</s>) the creation beginning with <s>pratyaya</s> (intellectual dispositions) is the creation of grace.
 That is indeed the <s>tanmātrasarga</s> (creation of subtle elements), also known by the alternative name <s>viśeṣa</s> (particulars).
 What are the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars) and how many are they?
 It is stated:
 The subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), the gross bodies (<s>sthūladeha</s>), and the gross elements (<s>sthūlabhūtāni</s>).
 Therein, the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), produced before the gross body, is unobstructed and imperishable even upon the destruction of the gross [body].

children.translated_text: The creation of beings is of fourteen kinds. <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 20.

body.text:
caturdaśavidho bhūtasargaḥ |
tatrāṣṭāvikalpo daivastairyagyonaḥ pañcadhā mānuṣya ekavidhaḥ brāhmaḥ prājāpatyaḥ paitre gāndharvo yākṣo rākṣasaḥ paiśācāśca daivasargaḥ paśumṛgasarīsṛpasthāvarāḥ tiraścāṃ sargaḥ |
brāhmaṇādijātibhede 'pi saṃsthāne viśeṣābhāvāt ekavidho mānuṣya iti caturdaśavidhāḥ sthūladehāḥ |
body.translated_text:
The creation of beings (<s>bhūtasarga</s>) is of fourteen kinds.
 Therein, the divine (<s>daiva</s>) creation is eightfold; the animal (<s>tairyagyona</s>) is fivefold; the human (<s>mānuṣya</s>) is of one kind. The <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Paitrya</s>, <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Yākṣa</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s> — these constitute the divine creation. Animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and stationary beings constitute the creation of the animal realm.
 Although there are distinctions of caste (<s>jāti</s>) such as <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and others, since there is no difference in bodily form, the human [creation] is of one kind — thus the gross bodies are of fourteen kinds.

children.translated_text: Bondage is of three kinds. <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 21.

body.text:
kaḥ punarbandhaḥ katidhā ca |
trividho bandhaḥ |
kāḥ punastā vidhā ucyante |
prākṛtiko vaikṛtiko dākṣaṇikaśca bandhaḥ |
prakṛtimātmānaṃ jñātvā taccintanāt prākṛtikaḥ atrocyate pūrṇavarṣasahasraṃ tu tiṣṭhantyavyaktacintakā iti |

children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Mahat</s> and the other [evolutes] as the self and contemplating them constitutes <s>vaikārika</s> (derivative) bondage.
Here it is said:
Those who contemplate the sense organs remain for ten <s>manvantaras</s>;
those devoted to the elements remain for a full hundred, and those identified with [the elements] for a thousand;

body.translated_text:
What then is bondage, and of how many kinds?
 Bondage is of three kinds.
 What are those kinds? It is stated:
 Bondage is <s>prākṛtika</s> (natural), <s>vaikṛtika</s> (derivative), and <s>dākṣaṇika</s> (meritorious).
 Knowing <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) as the self and contemplating it constitutes <s>prākṛtika</s> bondage. Here it is said: 'Those who contemplate the Unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) remain for a full thousand years.'

body.text: bauddhā daśasahasrāṇi tiṣṭhanti vigatajvarāḥ /
body.translated_text: those devoted to <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) remain for ten thousand, free from affliction.

body.text:
amī videhāḥ |
iṣṭāpūrttī dakṣiṇā tannimitto dākṣaṇikaḥ atrocyate /
svargasthā narakaṃ yānti nārakāśca triviṣṭapamiti /
body.translated_text:
These are the <s>videhas</s> (disembodied ones).
 <s>Iṣṭāpūrta</s> (meritorious acts and charitable works) and <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees) — bondage caused by these is <s>dākṣaṇika</s>. Here it is said:
 'Those in heaven go to hell, and those in hell go to the celestial realm.'

body.text:
gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhanta iti ca |
ata eva hi triṣvapi bandheṣu ekaikāpāye tatastato mokṣa iti |
body.translated_text:
Those who are desire-driven obtain the state of coming and going.
 For this very reason, in all three bondages, upon the removal of each one, there is liberation from that respective [bondage].

children.translated_text: Liberation is of three kinds. <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 22.

body.text:
trividho mokṣaḥ |
karmaṇo vikārāt prākṛtaśca mokṣaḥ |
yaduktam |
body.translated_text:
Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is of three kinds.
 Liberation from action (<s>karman</s>), from modification (<s>vikāra</s>), and <s>prākṛta</s> (natural) liberation.
 As it has been stated:

children.text: prākṛtena ca bandhena tathā vaikārikeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: By natural (<s>prākṛtena</s>) bondage, and likewise by derivative (<s>vaikārika</s>) bondage,
and by the third, meritorious bondage (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), one is bound and is not freed by any other [means].

body.text: iti |
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text:
atha kutastyānāṃ tattvānāṃ siddhiḥ |
pramāṇāditi brūmaḥ |
body.translated_text:
Now, how is the establishment of these principles achieved?
 We say: through the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

children.translated_text: The means of valid knowledge is threefold. <s>Tattvasamāsa</s> 23.

body.text:
tatra pramāṇaṃ kiṃ katividhama vā ucyate trividhaṃ pramāṇam |
tisro vidhā yasyeti trividham |
kāstā vidhāḥ |
ucyate |
dṛṣṭamanumānamāptavacanaṃ ca |
arthasannikṛṣṭendriyajo niścayo dṛṣṭam |
indriyāṇi pañca cakṣurādīni manaśca |
vyāptipakṣadharmatājñānapūrvakamanumānam |
tacca trividham |
pūrvavat śeṣavat sāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca |
pūrvavadyathā kardamena pūrvavṛttavṛṣṭyanumānam |
śeṣavadyathā |
samudrātapalamudakaṃ(?) kṣāramupalabhya śeṣasyāpi kṣāratvānumānam |
sāmānyato dṛṣṭāṃ ca yathā |
rūpādyupalabhya tadupalabdheḥ kāraṇasyānumānam |
rūpādyupalabdhayaḥ karaṇasādhyāḥ kriyatvāt chidikriyāvat |
āptaśrutirāptavacanaṃ ca |
yathārthavākyajārthaviṣayodhyavasāya iti yāvat |
prāvādukodbhāvitānāṃ tu upamānārthāpattisambhavābhāvaitihyapratibhānāmityukteṣvevāntarbhāvaḥ |
yat tadyathā gaurgavayastatheti vākyam |
tadjñānanidhīrāgama eva |
gavayepi gosadṛśasya gavayaśabdo vācaka iti pratyayaḥ soyamanumānametatsaṅketagraharūpatvāt |
yad gavayasya cakṣuḥsannikṛṣṭagosādṛśyajñānaṃ tatpratyakṣameva |
ata eva smaryamāṇāyāṃ gavi sādṛśyajñānaṃ pratyakṣam |
gogavayayoḥ sādṛśyasya gavayāntaravarttibhūyovayavasāmānyarūpasya yogarūpasyaikatvādityupamānaṃ na mānāntaram |
jīvato gṛhābhāvadarśanena bahirbhāvakalpanādityarthāpattiranumānameva |
sambhavopi khāryādau droṇāḍhakaprasthādyavagamarūpo 'numānameva |
iha bhūtale ghaṭo nāstītyādirabhāvāvagamo 'pi pratyakṣameveti nābhāvaḥ pṛthak pramāṇam |
anirdiṣṭapravaktṛkaṃ pravādamātramaitihyamapīha vaṭe yakṣaḥ prativasatītyapramāṇameva |
āptamūlatve tvāgama eva |
dvāravatī puṇyabhūmiriti śruteḥ tatra vasataḥ śreyāṃsastatra gamane puṇyaṃ bhavatītyādibuddhirjāyamānā pratibhā |
yatrocyate |

children.translated_text: 'A wise person intuits even what has not been [explicitly] stated.'
That [intuition], however, is generally a valid <s>pramāṇa</s> itself.
The vision of sages (<s>ārṣa darśana</s>) is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) itself.
And that intuition (<s>pratibhā</s>) is inference (<s>anumāna</s>) itself.

body.translated_text:
Now, what is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), and of how many kinds? It is said: <s>pramāṇa</s> is threefold.
That which has three kinds is 'threefold.'
What are those kinds?
It is said:
Perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and authoritative testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>).
The ascertainment born from a sense-organ in contact with an object is perception (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>).
The sense-organs are the five [beginning with] the eye and so forth, and the mind (<s>manas</s>).
Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is preceded by the knowledge of invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) and the property of the subject (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>).
And that is threefold:
<s>Pūrvavat</s> (from cause to effect), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from effect to cause), and <s>sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation).
<s>Pūrvavat</s> is, for example, the inference of [upcoming] rain from [seeing] muddy clouds, based on prior [experience].
<s>Śeṣavat</s> is, for example:
having observed that a portion of ocean water is salty, one infers that the remainder is also salty.
<s>Sāmānyato dṛṣṭa</s> (from general observation) is, for example:
having perceived form and other [qualities], the inference of a cause for that perception.
Perceptions of form and the like are accomplishable by an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), because they are actions — like the action of cutting.
Reliable scripture (<s>āptaśruti</s>) is authoritative testimony (<s>āptavacana</s>).
That is, the determinate cognition whose object is the meaning born from sentences conveying truth.
As for the [additional means] proposed by others — <s>upamāna</s> (analogy), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>sambhava</s> (inclusion), <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence), <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), and <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition) — these are subsumed within the [three] already stated.
Take for instance the statement 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow' —
the knowledge [from this] is rooted in scripture (<s>āgama</s>) alone.
The cognition that the word '<s>gavaya</s>' denotes something similar to a cow — that is inference itself, because it has the form of grasping a convention.
The knowledge of similarity to a cow arising from sense-contact with a <s>gavaya</s> — that is direct perception itself.
Therefore, the knowledge of similarity when a cow is being remembered is also perception.
Since the similarity between a cow and a <s>gavaya</s> is one — being of the nature of the universal form of the majority of parts present in other <s>gavayas</s> — therefore <s>upamāna</s> (analogy) is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.
<s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — inferring that one who is alive but absent from home must be outside — is inference itself.
<s>Sambhava</s> (inclusion) too — the understanding of <s>droṇa</s>, <s>āḍhaka</s>, <s>prastha</s>, and so forth within a <s>khārī</s> [measure] — is inference itself.
The cognition of absence (<s>abhāva</s>) such as 'there is no pot on this ground' is perception itself — therefore <s>abhāva</s> is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>.
Tradition (<s>aitihya</s>) — mere hearsay without an identified speaker, such as 'a <s>Yakṣa</s> dwells in this banyan tree' — is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all.
But if it has a reliable source, it is simply scripture (<s>āgama</s>).
From hearing that '<s>Dvāravatī</s> is a meritorious land,' the cognition that arises — 'there is merit in going there for one who dwells there seeking well-being' — that is <s>pratibhā</s> (intuition).
Regarding which it is said:

children.translated_text: Indeed, by twenty-three <s>sūtras</s>, the summary of all <s>śāstra</s> (philosophical science)
has been composed here by the foremost sage, to the best of [his] understanding, with a concise commentary.

body.text: iti sāṃkhyasūtravivaraṇākhyā kāpilasūtravṛttiḥ samāptā ||
body.translated_text: Thus concludes the commentary on the <s>Kāpila Sūtras</s> named <s>Sāṃkhyasūtravivaraṇa</s>.
